sentences.nl: Ik vraag straks aan Marieke, of ze met mij hierheen komt.
sentences.en: I'll ask Marieke later if she will come here with me.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I ask later to Marieke, if she with me here comes.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the verb "vragen" (to ask), which is followed by "aan" to indicate the person being asked.  
• The word "straks" means "later" and is used to indicate a future action.  
• The conjunction "of" introduces an indirect question or statement, translating to "if" or "whether" in English.  
• Note the verb-second rule in the Dutch main clause: "Ik vraag straks aan Marieke," followed by the subordinate clause "of ze met mij hierheen komt," where the verb "komt" appears at the end.

- Ik vraag aan de leraar, of hij me kan helpen. (I ask the teacher if he can help me.)
- Ze wil weten of hij morgen komt. (She wants to know if he is coming tomorrow.)
- Hij vraagt zich af of het mogelijk is. (He wonders if it is possible.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ik vertel morgen aan mijn vriend, dat ik verhuis. (I will tell my friend tomorrow that I am moving.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: Ik heb haar nog niet eens gekust,, maar… ik ben wel verliefd op Marieke!
sentences.en: I haven't even kissed her yet, but... I am in love with Marieke!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I have her yet not even kissed, but… I am indeed in love with Marieke!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present perfect tense "heb gekust" (have kissed) to describe an action that has not occurred yet. "Nog niet eens" is a phrase meaning "not even yet," adding emphasis to the fact that something has not happened.  
• "Wel" is used to indicate contrast or emphasis, similar to "indeed" or "actually" in English.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Ik heb hem nog niet eens gezien." (I have not even seen him yet.)  
  - "Ze is wel tevreden met het resultaat." (She is indeed satisfied with the result.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hij heeft zijn huiswerk nog niet eens afgemaakt, maar hij is wel trots op zijn werk." (He has not even finished his homework yet, but he is indeed proud of his work.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, expressing feelings openly, such as saying "ik ben verliefd" (I am in love), is generally acceptable and can reflect a direct and honest communication style.

sentences.nl: Maar dat heeft Lars me verteld!? — Misschien is het een misverstandje.
sentences.en: But that's what Lars told me!? — Maybe it's a misunderstanding.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But that has Lars me told!? — Maybe is it a misunderstanding.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Maar dat heeft Lars me verteld" uses the perfect tense with "heeft" (has) as the auxiliary verb. The past participle "verteld" (told) comes at the end of the clause, which is typical in Dutch subordinate clauses.  
• "Misschien is het een misverstandje" uses "misschien" (maybe) at the start of the sentence, which is common for indicating uncertainty. The diminutive "misverstandje" (little misunderstanding) softens the tone.  
• Extra Sentences:  
  - "Dat heeft ze me al eerder gezegd." (She has told me that before.)  
  - "Misschien is het een goed idee om te wachten." (Maybe it’s a good idea to wait.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Maar dat heeft Anna al geregeld!? — Misschien is het beter om te controleren." (But Anna has already arranged that!? — Maybe it's better to check.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch, using the diminutive form, like "misverstandje," can soften statements and make them sound less accusatory or harsh. This is a common way to maintain politeness and avoid confrontation in Dutch communication.

sentences.nl: Martin is boos op zijn vriend Gianluca,, maar hij moet ook huilen…
sentences.en: Martin is angry with his friend Gianluca, but he also has to cry…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Martin is angry at his friend Gianluca, but he must also cry...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Boos op" (angry at) is a common Dutch expression for being angry at someone, using the preposition "op."  
• "Moet" (must) is an auxiliary verb used to indicate necessity or obligation.  
• Word order: The conjunction "maar" (but) introduces a contrast and is followed by the subject "hij" (he).

Extra phrases:  
• "Zij is boos op haar broer." (She is angry at her brother.)  
• "Ik moet vandaag werken." (I must work today.)  
• "Hij is blij met zijn nieuwe fiets." (He is happy with his new bike.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Anna is teleurgesteld in haar team, maar ze moet doorgaan." (Anna is disappointed in her team, but she must continue.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific cultural note related to this sentence.

sentences.nl: Hij heeft liefdesverdriet.
sentences.en: He is lovesick.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He has love sorrow.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij" is the subject pronoun meaning "he."  
• "Heeft" is the third-person singular present tense of "hebben," meaning "to have."  
• "Liefdesverdriet" is a compound noun from "liefde" (love) and "verdriet" (sorrow), meaning "heartache" or "lovesickness."  
• Compound nouns are common in Dutch, often combining two or more words into one.

Examples:  
• Hij heeft hoofdpijn. (He has a headache.)  
• Zij heeft huiswerk. (She has homework.)  
• Ik heb een vraag. (I have a question.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hij heeft honger. (He is hungry.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch-speaking cultures, expressing emotions like "liefdesverdriet" can be more reserved than in some other cultures, but it is still a universally understood and relatable experience.

sentences.nl: Gelukkig is Xing bij hem, zodat ze hem kan troosten.
sentences.en: Fortunately, Xing is with him so she can comfort him.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Luckily is Xing by him, so-that she him can comfort.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "gelukkig" (luckily) to express a positive emotion or relief.  
• "Bij hem" means "by him" and indicates proximity or being with someone.  
• "Zodat" is a conjunction meaning "so that," introducing a purpose or result clause.  
• The sentence structure includes a subordinate clause introduced by "zodat," which causes inversion in the main clause.  
• Examples:  
  - Hij bleef thuis, zodat hij kon uitrusten. (He stayed home so that he could rest.)  
  - Zij is blij dat hij bij haar is. (She is happy that he is with her.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Gelukkig is Anna bij ons, zodat we samen kunnen werken. (Luckily, Anna is with us, so that we can work together.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: Wat jammer voor Martin.
sentences.en: What a pity for Martin.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• What a pity for Martin.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wat jammer" is an idiomatic expression in Dutch that translates to "What a pity" or "That's too bad" in English. "Wat" is the Dutch word for "what," and "jammer" means "pity" or "unfortunate."  
• "Voor" means "for" and is used to indicate the person affected by the situation.  
• The sentence structure is straightforward: exclamatory phrase + preposition + person's name.

• Additional examples:  
  - Wat jammer dat ze niet kon komen. (What a pity that she couldn't come.)  
  - Wat jammer dat het regent. (What a pity that it is raining.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Wat jammer voor de kinderen. (What a pity for the children.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• (No cultural note applicable.)

sentences.nl: Hij verlangde zo naar dit moment.
sentences.en: He longed so much for this moment.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He longed so for this moment.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij verlangde" is in the past tense, from the verb "verlangen" (to long or yearn).  
• "Zo" is an adverb meaning "so" or "very," used for emphasis.  
• The preposition "naar" is used with "verlangen" to indicate what someone is longing for.  
– Ik verlang naar vakantie. (I long for a holiday.)  
– Zij verlangde naar het einde van de dag. (She longed for the end of the day.)  
– Wij verlangen naar een betere toekomst. (We long for a better future.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij verlangde zo naar een warm kopje thee. (She longed so much for a warm cup of tea.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, expressing longing or yearning is often related to anticipation of something positive or comforting, like a holiday or a warm drink, reflecting a value placed on comfort and enjoyment.
